annotation.summary_en: Two elderly men play backgammon and brag about their outings, leading to a punchline about one man's failing memory regarding his wife's name.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch takes place in a sunny orchard yard where two men are seated at an outdoor table covered with a cloth and a fruit bowl, playing a lively game of backgammon. One man, wearing a gray jacket and eyeglasses, recounts a disappointing trip to a strip club in Moscow with his grandson, complaining that the poles blocked his view. The other man, dressed in a blazer, counters by boasting about a wonderful three-hour dinner his son treated him and his wife to at a fancy restaurant. When asked for the name of the restaurant, the second man struggles to remember. In a roundabout attempt to jog his memory, he asks his friend for the name of a thorny flower with a red bud. When the friend provides the word 'Rose' (Vard), the man turns to his wife (a woman in a patterned robe standing nearby) and shouts, 'Vard, what was the name of that restaurant yesterday?', revealing he had forgotten his own wife's name while trying to recall the venue.
catchphrases: ես իրա ցավը տանեմ, տարել էր ինձ ու պարավիս ռեստորան
